# ORTYO

> ORTYO is a programmable integration boundary for observing, controlling, replaying, and verifying how software interacts with the outside world.

## Canonical interfaces

- MCP: run `ortyo mcp`; always call `initialize` and `tools/list` before relying on tool names or schemas.
- CLI: `ortyo ...`; successful command output is structured JSON.
- Local HTTP API: canonical local Boundary, Exposure, Scenario, Recording, Contract, Assertion, and Interaction APIs.
- Hosted HTTP API: workspace-scoped Exposure and bounded outbound HTTP execution APIs.

## Core model

- Boundary - executable edge between an application and an external dependency.
- Session - runtime grouping of related interactions.
- Interaction - canonical evidence of what crossed a Boundary.
- Exposure - controlled reachability through an ORTYO Boundary.
- Recording - immutable captured evidence for replay.
- Contract - assertions over observed interactions.
- Scenario - reusable setup + evidence + replay + assertion workflow.

Do not model ORTYO as a VM, Devbox, sandbox, or generic tunnel provider. Compute providers are implementation details behind execution/runtime boundaries.

## Default agent workflow

For integration verification, prefer:

`scenario_create -> scenario_start -> exercise application behavior -> scenario_complete -> scenario_outcome_get`

For lower-level evidence work, use Exposure -> Interactions -> Recording -> Replay -> Contract -> Assertion.

Use MCP when available because `tools/list` is the authoritative machine-readable tool schema. Use CLI structured JSON when MCP is unavailable.

## Security invariants

- Never print, return, log, or paste raw ORTYO tokens, runtime capabilities, or captured secret values.
- Prefer typed `ortyo://secrets/...` SecretRefs for hosted execution.
- Typed SecretRefs are workspace-scoped and bound to an allowed HTTP origin; wrong-origin use fails closed.
- Public Exposure URLs are reachability, not authentication credentials.
- Runtime capabilities are separate, short-lived credentials for a specific Exposure.
- Hosted outbound execution permits bounded HTTP/HTTPS only and rejects unsafe destinations and redirects.
- Do not bypass ORTYO policy by reaching directly into secret storage or provider-specific infrastructure.

## Approval-gated hosted execution

For sensitive hosted actions, prefer the one-shot approval flow:

`POST /_ortyo/hosted/approvals -> inspect -> approve/deny -> POST /_ortyo/hosted/approvals/{id}/execute`

The asking/acting credential needs `requests:execute`. The deciding credential needs the separate `requests:approve` scope. Approval is bound to the exact canonical request digest, stores only a redacted summary, and is consumed before the outbound attempt. Never treat an approval ID as authorization for a modified request.

## Failure semantics

Hosted execution distinguishes:
- succeeded - structured ExecutionEvidence exists;
- rejected - ORTYO rejected the attempted action under its request/security contract;
- failed - provider/runtime work did not produce valid successful evidence.

Every recorded execution attempt has a UUIDv7 execution_id, workspace_id, provider kind, and start/completion timestamps.
